result.stdout:
Usage: clip [options]

Cross-platform clipboard bridge — copy from stdin, paste to stdout, clear.

Options:
  -c, --copy                   Force copy mode (read stdin to clipboard), overriding autodetect
  -p, --paste                  Force paste mode (read clipboard to stdout), overriding autodetect
  --clear                      Empty the clipboard, overriding autodetect
  -r, --raw                    Do not strip trailing newline on paste
  --primary                    Target X11/Wayland PRIMARY selection (Linux only; ignored elsewhere)
  -h, --help                   Show help
  --version                    Show version
  --no-color                   Disable colored output
  --json                       JSON output
  --describe                   Structured JSON metadata for AI agents
  --color[=auto|always|never]  Coloured output: auto (default when omitted), always, or never

Examples:
  clip                      Paste clipboard contents to stdout
  echo hello | clip         Copy 'hello' to the clipboard (trailing newline preserved in copy)
  clip --clear              Empty the clipboard
  clip -r > out.txt         Paste without stripping trailing newline
  clip --primary            Paste from the Linux PRIMARY selection (middle-click buffer)
  echo hi | clip --primary  Copy to the Linux PRIMARY selection (applies to copy and clear too)

Composes with:
  ids | clip                                    Generate an ID and copy it to the clipboard
  digest report.txt | clip                      Copy a file hash to the clipboard (sha256 default)
  qr "https://example.com" --format svg | clip  Copy an SVG-encoded QR payload to the clipboard

Exit Codes:
  0    Success (including empty-clipboard paste)
  125  Invalid flags / conflicting modes / invalid UTF-8 input
  126  Clipboard busy or helper failure
  127  No clipboard helper found (Linux only)
